article_summary: Anthropic researchers report that an internal Claude model recovered the origins of five NIST prime-curve seeds in under half an hour, and five ANSI X9.62 seeds show the same pattern. The seeds were not passphrase hashes, as a 2015 tip suggested, but outputs of the C library **lrand48** generator initialized with Unix timestamps between May 1997 and April 1998.Claude recognized the generator from zero top bits, recovered truncated states with lattice reduction, and reproduced each 160-bit seed, matching six base points to FreeLIP seeds. The work does not demonstrate a cryptographic break, and Anthropic says it makes deliberate backdoors less plausible. The P-224, P-256, P-384 and P-521 base points, the B-163 seed, and the criteria for skipping viable candidates remain unexplained.
